To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PGE(2)-induced inhibition of AVT-induced increase of OWP is mediated by EP(1) receptors, activation of the NO-cGMP pathway, and nNOS in the frog R. temporaria urinary bladder.
PGE(2)-EP(1)-receptors activate the NO/cGMO pathway in epithelial cells of frog urinary bladder, which leads to the inhibition of AVT-induced Osmotic Water Permeability (OWP).

PGE(2)-induced inhibition of AVT-induced increase of osmolyte permeability is based at least on EP(1) receptor-mediated activation of NO and cGMP production in epithelial cells of the frog urinary bladder.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms underlying PGE(2)-induced inhibition of AVT-induced Osmotic water permeability.
the mechanisms underlying the effect of PGE on the AVT-induced Osmotic water permeability.
the mechanisms of PGE(1) receptor-mediated inhibition of vasotocin (VT)-induced osmotic water permeabilization (OWP) by PGE(1).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

PGE(2)-mediated inhibition of AVT-induced OMP in the frog urinary epithelial cells is based at least in part on EP1-receptor activation and subsequent stimulation of the NO/cAMP pathway, and this may have important implications in the regulation of the water transport in the frog urinary bladders.
PGE(2)-induced NO production in the frog bladder epithelium is a mechanism of PGE(1) receptor-mediated inhibition of AVT-induced osmotic water transport.

the inhibitory action of PGE(1) on AVT-mediated increase of osmotic permeability in the urinary bladder is based on EP(1) receptor-mediated activation of the nitric oxide/cyclic guanosine monophosphate pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PGE(2)-induced activation of the EP(1) receptor leads to an increase in NO production, and that this increase in NO production leads to a reduction in AVT-induced Osmotic Water Permeability.
PGE2 inhibits AVT-induced osmotic water flow by EP1 receptor-mediated activation of NO-cGMP pathway in frog urinary bladder epithelium.
PGE(2)-induced activation of the NO-cGMP pathway in epithelial cells inhibits vasotcin-induced osmotic water transport in the frog urinary bladders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inhibitory effects of PGE(1) on vasotocin (a hormone that regulates osmotic water permeabilty) induced OWP in frog urinary bladders are mediated by activation of the NO-cGMP pathway.
the inhibitory action of PGE(1) on AVT-activated osmotic water transport in the frog urinary epithelium is mediated by the NO/cGAMP pathway.
PGE(2)-induced inhibition of AVT-induced OMP in the frog urinary epithelium is mediated through activation of the EP(1)-NOS/cGMP pathway.
